speaker_role: Common App staff member (Brian, described as 'part of the CommonApp team')
commercial_incentive: None evident beyond promoting Common App's own platform/resources (official product walkthrough, not a paid third-party service)
key_insights: The Common App activities section is filled out once and shared across every school a student applies to via that platform
Students can include activities dating back to the start of high school; returning/older applicants should generally include activities no more than about 10 years old
Each activity gets a 150-character description that should specify concrete contributions, accomplishments, and any leadership positions or awards
If more space is needed, students can use the separate 'additional information' section of the application
Students report estimated hours per week per activity, and can use an average if time commitment fluctuates across the year

Family responsibilities (childcare, eldercare, household tasks, contributing to family income) can be listed as an activity, since colleges want to understand their effect on a student's time for academics/other activities
Up to 10 activities can be listed, but the section is not about maximizing the count - it should focus on which activities best represent the student and what has been most meaningful to them
specific_numbers_or_facts: Activity descriptions are limited to 150 characters (per Common App)
Up to 10 activities can be listed in the section, but using all 10 is not required (per Common App)
Rule of thumb: activities more than about 10 years old generally should not be included for returning/older applicants (per Common App)
notable_or_distinctive: Coming directly from Common App itself, this is an authoritative, official walkthrough of the platform's own mechanics (character limits, hours reporting, inclusion of family responsibilities) rather than third-party interpretation.
reliability_notes: Content is short, generic promotional/how-to material from the platform itself rather than admissions strategy advice; no discussion of how officers actually weigh or read this section (that nuance is covered more in other, longer videos in this batch).
